proposals.evidence: DEDR 5151 directly documents the corresponding who forms: Brahui dēr, Gondi bor, Kannada yār, Kodagu/Kota dār, Kurukh nē, Malayalam ār, Malto né, Parji ēd, Tamil yār, Telugu evaru, Toda ōry and Tulu ērů. Source cognacy explicitly identifies this article. Final vowels and Malto -du are retained as surveyed morphological variants, not removed. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4885 directly groups the mīn fish series in Kannada, Kodagu, Kota, Tamil, Tulu and Malto (mínu). The survey final -ə and Malto -du are retained. Badaga and Ravula are comparative extensions explicitly labelled look-alikes by the upstream annotation; neither is falsely described as listed in DEDR. The article’s Sanskrit mīna comparison does not itself specify a loan route for these records. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 410(a) documents the proximal demonstrative i- series: Kannada idu/itu, Kodagu idï, Kota id, Kuwi īdi, Malayalam/Parji ī, Malto íth, Gadaba id, Tamil inta and Telugu idi. The upstream survey annotation identifies this article. Betta Kurumba idə is a comparative extension, explicitly only a look-alike in that annotation; no claim of a literal dictionary attestation for Betta Kurumba is made. Existing parent *iH- represents subsection (a), not the today/still/small formations in later subsections. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 561 documents Kannada ugur, Kodagu oy, Gondi gōr, Kurukh orox, Kuwi gōru with plural gōrka, Malto orgu and Toda ǖr as the nail/claw family. Survey final vowels and plural-looking material remain unchanged. Badaga ugilə is a comparative extension explicitly described as a look-alike in the source; Kodagu voyi and Toda yūr retain their initial glide/transcription differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 474 explicitly documents Kannada eraḍu, Kodagu daṇḍï, Kota eyḏ, Kurukh irb (two persons), Kuwi rindi, Malayalam raṇṭu, Parji adjectival ir, Tamil reṇṭu and Toda ēḍ. The survey cognacy annotations independently identify the article. Final vowels and the Kurukh personal versus Parji adjectival use are retained; no grammatical category is silently added to the generic survey gloss two. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
